questions.prompt: Pope St. Leo the Great's letter, known as the 'Tome of Leo,' played a decisive role at which 451 council in defining Christ's two natures?
choices: The Council of Chalcedon
The Council of Ephesus
The Council of Nicaea
The Council of Trent
questions.explanation: Though he never attended in person, Leo's Tome was read at Chalcedon and shaped its definition that Christ is one Person in two natures, fully divine and fully human.
questions.hint: This pope never attended the council in person, but his letter settled the debate.

citations.quote: To be acknowledged in two natures, without confusion, without change, without division, without separation... concurring in one Person and one Subsistence.

questions.prompt: True or False: St. Maximus the Confessor suffered the amputation of his tongue and right hand for refusing to accept Monothelitism, the teaching that Christ had only one will.
questions.explanation: Maximus insisted Christ possessed both a divine and a human will, in keeping with his two full natures -- a teaching later affirmed at the Third Council of Constantinople, after Maximus had already suffered for it.
questions.hint: The Church later vindicated his exact position at the Third Council of Constantinople -- after his mutilation, not before.

citations.quote: two natural volitions or wills in him and two natural principles of action which undergo no division, no change, no partition, no confusion... his human will following, and not resisting or struggling, rather in fact subject to his divine and all powerful will.

questions.prompt: St. Vincent of Lérins offered a test for identifying authentic tradition. What was it?
choices: What has been believed everywhere, always, and by all — universality, antiquity, and consent
Whatever the majority of bishops hold at a given moment
Whatever can be found explicitly in Scripture
Whatever the oldest available manuscript supports
questions.correctAnswer: What has been believed everywhere, always, and by all — universality, antiquity, and consent
questions.explanation: Quod ubique, quod semper, quod ab omnibus. Vincent knew the test needed qualification, since doctrine visibly develops, and he addressed that too — growth in understanding is legitimate so long as it is growth in the same sense and the same judgement, not a change into something else.
questions.hint: Three tests: where, when, and by whom.

questions.prompt: True or False: St. Ephrem the Syrian, a Doctor of the Church, wrote most of his theology in hymns rather than treatises.
questions.explanation: True. Ephrem taught doctrine in sung poetry in Syriac, and the Church has recognised it as theology by naming him a Doctor. It is a useful counterweight to the assumption that serious theology must be argumentative prose — the same instinct behind the Church's Latin hymns.
questions.hint: His medium was the same one the Church still uses at Vespers.

questions.prompt: St. John Damascene's defence of images rested on a specifically Christological argument. What was it?
choices: The invisible God has become visible in the flesh, so depicting the incarnate Christ affirms rather than violates the Incarnation
Images are permitted because most believers were illiterate
The commandment against images applied only to the Old Covenant as a legal matter
Images may be venerated because they sometimes work miracles
questions.correctAnswer: The invisible God has become visible in the flesh, so depicting the incarnate Christ affirms rather than violates the Incarnation
questions.explanation: He turns the objection into a Christological test: to refuse an image of Christ is, at the limit, to doubt that God really took visible flesh. That is why iconoclasm was answered as a question about the Incarnation rather than about art.
questions.hint: Before the Incarnation, God truly was invisible -- ask what that means for whether an image could ever have been allowed, and why that changed.
